qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dense Southeastern branch network and primary operating bank status for retail and commercial clients establish meaningful switching costs. Sticky low-cost deposit franchise ($131B+ deposits, substantial non-interest bearing mix) supports 14-18% historical ROATCE and low deposit beta. Primary erosion risks stem from fintech digital disintermediation, deposit competition from money market yields and money-center banks, and regulatory scrutiny on non-interest fee income.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). Regions Financial operates an entrenched Southeastern retail and commercial banking franchise with sticky low-cost deposits and switching costs (Gates 1-5 pass), but fails Gate 6 under the structural commercial fractional-reserve bank standard (g6_default: N). Financial leverage of ~9-10x on common equity ($158.8B total assets vs. ~$18.0B common equity) entails inherent asset-liability duration mismatch and deposit duration risk. Because commercial banks fundamentally rely on continuous rollover of confidence-sensitive deposits and external liquidity backstops, the balance sheet fails Charlie Munger's peace-of-mind fortress standard requiring zero reliance on the kindness of strangers.
qualitative.evidence: FY2025 consolidated assets of $158.8B and deposits of $131.1B against $18.0B common equity (~8.8x asset leverage, >10x total liabilities/equity). Capitalization remains sound by regulatory standards with CET1 ratio of 10.89% (FY2025) and 10.80% (FY2024). Net interest margin and ROE (10.0% in FY2025, 12.7% in FY2024; ROATCE ~14-18%) benefit from low-cost Sunbelt deposit density, but fractional-reserve maturity transformation creates structural deposit duration risk and exposure to yield curve shifts, resulting in default Gate 6 failure for commercial deposit banks.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
